title: What is a physical image?
quick: A physical image is a sector-by-sector copy of a whole storage device, including deleted data, unused space and areas outside any file system. On phones, it means a raw copy of the device memory.

sections.title: What it contains
text: A physical image copies the device from the first sector to the last, without looking at the file system. It includes files, deleted data that is not overwritten yet, slack space, unallocated space, partition tables and boot areas. SWGDE describes it as a bitstream copy of the device.

sections.title: Why it is useful
text: Because nothing is skipped, an examiner can later recover deleted files, carve data and study the partition layout. It also keeps a full record of the device state at the time of copying. It needs as much storage as the device, unless the image is compressed, and it takes longer than copying files.

sections.title: Physical images of phones
text: For phones, NIST describes physical methods as extracting an image of the memory itself, such as with hex dumping, JTAG or chip-off. These methods reach deeper data but are more technical and invasive. Encryption and locks often limit what the image contains, so a physical image of a modern phone may be unreadable without keys.

example: A suspect's external hard drive is imaged sector by sector. Weeks later the examiner finds a deleted spreadsheet in unallocated space and a second, unused partition. A file copy would have shown neither.
mistakes: Calling any copy made with an imaging tool a physical image, even if only some files were selected.
Believing a physical image of a phone always includes deleted data.
Imaging a partition and calling it a full physical image of the disk.
Ignoring that hidden areas such as HPA may not be copied.
Forgetting to verify with a hash.

terms.meaning: A copy of every bit of data, in the same order as the source.
Space the file system does not currently use for a file. It may still hold old data.
Unused bytes at the end of the last block used by a file.
Removing a memory chip from a device and reading it directly.

exam.q: How does a physical image differ from a logical image?
exam.a: A physical image copies every sector, including deleted and unused areas. A logical image copies chosen files and folders through the file system.

exam.q: Why can a physical image on a phone still be hard to use?
exam.a: Phone storage is often encrypted, so the raw data may be unreadable without the right keys.

exam.q: When would you pick a logical image anyway?
exam.a: When time or storage is limited, when only certain data is in scope, or when a physical copy is not possible. Follow your lab's procedure.
